name: Angel
description: Angels are the embodiment of law, purity, and order. Their enemies cannot defy them. Angels will find you, hunt you, and destroy you. Angels are a controlling, defensive Archetype. They specialize in durability and tenacity, and it is a focused tenacity. Angels pick an enemy and they make that enemy's life real difficult. They are excellent Saboteurs, but can also play a solid Harrier or Attrition game. Angels don't dish out a lot of damage, but they can reliably withstand a ton of it, and they Challenge their enemies to focus on the Angel before they can deal with her friends. The Angel's Ability heals her every turn, so Angels cannot be Taken Out by HP loss while anyone else on her team is still standing. Angels make heavy use of Challenge tokens, using them to control their enemies, and every Style they have gives them a different means of dealing with having a lot of enemies who all want you dead.
focused: Your Challenges are Unblockable By Shields.
At the start of your turn, you may heal, then if you did, Challenge an enemy you can see and deal 1 damage to them.
After you Challenge an enemy, deal 1 damage to them and heal 1.
fused: Your Challenges are Unblockable By Shields.
At the start of your turn, you may heal 2, then if you did, Challenge an enemy you can see.
After you Challenge an enemy, you deal 1 damage to them.
frantic: Your Challenges are Unblockable By Shields.
At the start of this turn, you may heal, then if you did, Challenge an enemy you can see and deal 1 damage to them.
Until your next turn, after you Challenge an enemy, deal 1 damage to them and heal 1.

actions.name: Siren Song
actions.text:
Challenge one enemy you can see. You may Pull them up to 3.
5+: Challenge every enemy adjacent to the initial target, then Pull 1 to everyone Challenged by Siren Song.

notes: The second half of the Focused Angel Ability does trigger off of the first half. The end result is that at the start of your turn, you Challenge an enemy, deal 2 damage to them, and heal equal to the Heal Value +1. The second half of the Fused Angel Ability does also trigger off of the first half. The end result is that at the start of your turn, you Challenge an enemy, deal 1 damage to them, and heal 2.

styles.name: Halcyon
abilities: At the start of your turn, you may discard one token you hold.
After you discard tokens using an Action or Ability, you gain an equal number of Iron tokens.

actions.name: Purify
actions.text:
Discard one token from an ally within range.
3+: Discard up to two tokens from someone within range.
6+: Discard up to two tokens from someone within range.

styles.description: Halcyon Style is focused on Iron tokens and support, so it pairs well with defensive and support Forms. Paying for Token Actions does not count as removing tokens for Halcyon's Ability.
styles.recommended: Vigilance and Song are the only Forms that can remove tokens without Purify, allowing them to trigger Halcyon's Ability more often and more easily. Halcyon Iron is an extremely hard to kill supporting stance, with easy access to a massive stack of Iron tokens, Armor that regenerates Iron tokens when popped, and a support kit to protect your allies, too. Halcyon Blaster allows for very wide-reaching Purifies. Your extra targets can apply to any part of the Action, so an Amplified 6+ Purify could remove as many as 9 tokens!

styles.name: Judgment
abilities: When an enemy with your Challenge token starts their turn, they do not roll their lowest Action Die. It is discarded and unused. If they are in a Stance that does not roll Action Dice, they get rid of their bonus die, if they have one, or their smallest number, if they do not.
If an enemy discards your Challenge token using an enemy Action or Ability, all numbers currently in their Action Pool are reduced by 2 (to a minimum of 1).

actions.name: Denial
actions.text: Teleport into an empty space adjacent to an enemy you can see, then Challenge them.

styles.description: Judgment Style is great for singling out one enemy and making it hard for them to do anything. Reminder: Abilities do not work while you are Taken Out, so once you go down, Challenged enemies will no longer lose an Action Die at the start of their turns, and they may remove your Challenge token safely.
styles.recommended: Judgment Power can reliably use Denial, which covers for Power Form's mobility problem. A sudden, cross-map Crush can do a lot to help you win a fight. Judgment Iron and Judgment Reversal give you Armor, as well as other defensive benefits, letting you Challenge many enemies and survive the attention. Judgment Control is one of the hardest lock-down Stances in the game, letting you remove two of an enemy's Actions per turn at the cost of one Challenge and 1 Control token per enemy. Control tokens also give you the flexibility to decide which of their Actions to negate, as they declare it, and if they spend the time to use Put It Out on your Challenge, that's a third Action gone. Judgment Control is extremely rude. Judgment Thorns helps your Shields survive through your Challenged enemies' turns by limiting their Actions, and the Thorns Ability makes Challenged enemies defeat themselves for you.

styles.name: Shining
abilities: At the start of your turn, Push 1 to all obstacles and enemies adjacent to you.
Enemies cannot use Action Movement, Free Movement, or teleports to enter a space adjacent to you.
If an enemy discards your Challenge token using an enemy Action or Ability, the enemy who held the token takes 3 damage.

actions.name: Beacon
actions.text:
Pull up to 4 to an ally you can see, other than yourself.
4+, Once per turn: You and that ally heal.

actions.name: Blinding Light
actions.text:
Challenge an adjacent enemy, then Push 1 and give them 1 Burning token.
5+: Instead, Push 3 and give them 3 Burning tokens.

styles.description: Shining Style lets you act as a living wall, completely shutting down enemies limited to Range: 1, especially after you Challenge them. Anyone who tries to ignore or remove your Challenge will suffer blinding pain.
styles.recommended: Shining Vigilance and Shining Song generate a lot of breathing room, providing both healing and safety. Song provides you and your allies with buffs as a bonus, while Vigilance weakens your enemies. Shining Dance and Shining Shadow are hard to catch, making it extremely tempting for your foe to discard your Challenge some other way, but if they do, the power of the sun will burn them for their arrogance. Shining Control and Shining Blaster increase your range, allowing you to attack from behind the safety of the Shining Ability. Without this range boost, you have to move close enough to where enemies can hit you to attack them.

styles.name: Singing
abilities: At the start of your turn, choose a Mood: Despair, Sorrow, or Rage.
If you picked Despair, give 1 Fatigue token to all enemies.
If you picked Sorrow, give 1 Weakness token to all enemies.
If you picked Rage, give 1 Burning token to all enemies.

actions.name: Rip Chord
actions.text:
Give one of your Mood's tokens to an enemy within Range.
5+: Give one of your Mood's tokens to each enemy within Range.
8+: Give one of your Mood's tokens to each enemy you can see.

actions.name: Mood Shift
actions.text:
Apply all of your Start Effects as this Action's effects.
Usable once per turn, only during your own turn.

styles.description: Singing Style sings a dour song that weakens all enemies, and has a strong tendency to change the mood frequently. Mood Shift applies ALL of your "start of turn" effects as its Action. Any Ability that triggers during Phase 2: Start Phase will be triggered again, as Mood Shift's effect. This includes your current Archetype Ability, your current Form Ability, the Singing Ability, and your Build. As such, this Style pairs well with Archetypes and Forms with good start of turn Abilities, like Angel, Cavalry, Cyborg, Phantom, Punk, Vigilance Form, Wild Form, and especially Song Form.
styles.recommended: If you are in Singing Song Stance, Mood Shift lets you choose both your Song and Mood, and applies both (new) Start of Turn effects. Singing Vigilance can use Mood Shift for additional heal or token discard, depending on your needs. It also lets you pile on additional Weakness tokens, making Sorrow a good mood choice. It is generally better to stack one type of Status on a foe you want to disable, than to give them a one or two of each type.

styles.name: Winged
abilities: You do not take Fall Damage.
Rubble does not give you Fatigue tokens.
At the end of every turn, you may move 1 space.
After you give an enemy your Challenge token, you may Move 2.

actions.name: As The Crow Flies
actions.text:
Teleport 4.
4+: Challenge an enemy within range, then Teleport 2.

styles.description: Winged Style is a highly mobile harassment style, able to be anywhere it needs to be to best cause trouble. The Winged Ability triggers on every turn, not just your own, letting you stay out of reach.
styles.recommended: Winged Power, Winged Blaster, and Winged One-Two let you put that speed to good use, getting wherever you need to be to hurt things. Winged Reversal takes advantage of both parts' strengths, with Winged Style's free movement at the end of every turn putting you in position for Reversal Form's out of turn Actions. Winged's immunities combined with Reversal's Armor makes for a very good utility stance. Winged Shadow is possibly the fastest stance in the game, letting you constantly move around while creating obstacles as you go. If you want to be truly uncatchable, nothing gives you more off-turn mobility.

supers.name: Heaven's Piledriver
supers.effect: Deal 6 damage to an adjacent enemy. That enemy cannot use Free Movement until after the end of their next turn.
supers.description: The Angel's Alpha Super inflicts massive damage on a single target and slams them into the dirt so hard, they can't move. Even if they survive the attack, they aren't going anywhere anytime soon.

supers.name: Siren's Scream
supers.effect: Challenge and deal 2 damage to all enemies. Then, you gain an 8-point Shield.
supers.description: The Angel's Delta Super is the ultimate in drawing aggro. Enemies must focus on you, and they will have trouble breaking through the massive shield you've put together. Excellent when paired with Thorns Form, so your foes take damage for breaking through your mighty shield.

name: Cavalry
description: No one keeps up like the Cavalry. Your job is to get in, exactly where you need to be, and keep everyone on their feet. Nobody is there for them like you can be. Cavalry are protectors, heroes, and all around nice people to have on your side of the battlefield. Cavalry provide a wide variety of support abilities for their team, giving Shields to anyone who fights alongside them. The Cavalry can get wherever they need to be and provide just the back up your team needs. This makes them excellent Harriers, with solid Growth potential. Cavalry need to watch their positioning. Many of their Abilities work by being within range of their allies, and being where you need to be can make a huge difference in the flow of battle. Cavalry are all about the team buffs. When you have the Cavalry around, you can expect to get a bunch of small bonuses every turn. When playing as the Cavalry, be sure to keep track of these bonuses for your team, so they can properly take advantage of them.
focused: At the start and end of your turn, you may Move up to 2, then you and each ally within range gains Shield 2.
fused: At the start of your turn, you may Move up to 2, then you and each ally within range gains Shield 2.
frantic: At the start and end of this turn, you may Move up to 2, then you and each ally within range gains Shield 2.

actions.name: First Aid
actions.text:
Target an ally within Range 1-5. Pull yourself towards them, 1 space at a time, until you are adjacent to that ally.
4+: Heal that ally.
6+: Give that ally Shield 4. First Aid can only target an ally once per turn.

notes: The Pull granted by First Aid does not need to be in a totally straight line. You can curve it, so to speak. As long as each space of movement is closer to your target than the previous, it is a valid option. This is especially important because Rubble or Pits will end this movement prematurely, and Pits or Traps will damage you if you rush over them. Avoiding those obstacles is crucial to being a good medic. Shields cannot stack. If you give the 6+ First Aid shield to someone who already held a Shield, they must choose to either take the new Shield, or increase their existing Shield by 1.

styles.name: Charging
abilities: At the start of your turn, you gain temporary Armor and may Move up to 2.
At the start of each ally's turn, that ally may Move up to 2.

actions.name: Follow My Lead
actions.text:
You may move 1, then deal 1 damage to an enemy within range. An ally you can see (other than yourself) may move 1, then deal 1 damage to an enemy within their range.
6+: You may move 1, then deal 1 damage to an enemy within range. An ally you can see (other than yourself) may move 1, then deal 1 damage to an enemy within their range.

styles.description: Charging Style provides team support regardless of your own positioning, so its ideal for getting your team where they need to be. You are your own ally, so the Charging Ability to move at the start of each ally's turn includes you, on your own turn. When it is your turn, you will get to Move up to 4 spaces and gain temporary Armor. Temporary Armor is used after all other Armor and only triggers once. Once your temporary Armor has triggered, it is lost. Temporary Armor is a binary - you either have it or you do not. You cannot have multiple instances of temporary Armor.
styles.recommended: One-Two Form is a natural pair with Charging Style, even when it isn't your One-Two Form. An ally using One-Two will trigger the One- Two Ability when they Follow Your Lead. Be on the lookout for allies with other Abilities that trigger when they deal damage with an Action. Charging Blaster is a powerful combination. Each extra target for Follow My Lead can be an extra ally moving and attacking, letting the whole team strike in unison. Charging Shadow puts its six Action Dice to use, letting you use Follow My Lead many times. Charging Iron and Charging Power benefit from Charging Style's sheer quantity of Action Movement, to get around their Speed problems.

styles.name: Heroic
abilities: At the start of your turn, you heal 1.
Whenever an ally within range takes damage, they take half that damage (rounded down) and you take the other half (rounded up).

actions.name: Burning Heart
actions.text:
Each ally within range gains 2 Iron tokens and 2 Power tokens.
Usable once per turn, only while you hold no Power tokens.

actions.name: Hero's Moment
actions.text:
Deal 4 damage to an adjacent enemy and Push them X.
X is equal to 2, or to half the damage on your current health bar, rounded up, whichever is higher.

styles.description: Heroic Style keeps everyone else safe, no matter what. As long as you're in the middle of the squad, they will barely get hurt at all. If multiple allies with Heroic Style are within range of an ally who took damage, only one of them gets to use the Heroic Ability to redirect that damage. They must choose between them who takes half the hit. You are your own ally, so Burning Heart will also give 2 Iron tokens and 2 Power tokens to yourself.
styles.recommended: Heroic Iron and Heroic Reversal are obvious choices, as Armor drastically increases the Heroic Ability's benefits. Heroic Shadow can keep their Speed tokens between turns, so you can move to where you need to be to take damage. Shadow Form also lets you escape with Stunt if you start getting too badly hurt, while Reversal allows you to throw an off-turn interception. Heroic Thorns is a punishing stance. If you're positioned right, the Thorns Ability will deal damage to your enemies every time they attack anyone on your team, as long as you can keep your Shields up. Heroic Control is less obvious than other choices, but Range 1-5 with Burning Heart is a powerful combo. The Control tokens also help you deal with those attacks that you can't afford to take head on. Heroic Power cares less about the ability to protect their team, and more about using Hero's Moment to launch someone across the map.

styles.name: Jumping
abilities: At the start and end of your turn, you may Teleport 3.
When you Bleed, you may Teleport 3.

actions.name: Leap In
actions.text: Teleport 3. Then, deal 2 damage to an enemy within range.

actions.name: Leap Out
actions.text: Deal 2 damage to an enemy within range, then teleport 3. Then, choose one: Deal 2 damage to a different enemy within range; -or- heal 2; -or- gain 2 Power tokens.

styles.description: Jumping Style lets you dive onto threats that need to go down quickly, then leap back out of the fray after you're done. Sometimes the best team support is to take out the problem yourself. Teleportation is a type of movement that ignores all intervening space. "Teleport three spaces" effectively means "directly enter any space within range 1-3." You do not take fall damage from Pits or gain Fatigue tokens from Rubble you teleport to, but you do trigger Traps.
styles.recommended: Jumping Power and Jumping One-Two are obvious choices, as these Forms give you the damage you want when you dive onto a threat. Power Form always appreciates extra mobility, and One-Two Form loves cheap damage-dealing Actions. Jumping Blaster is also an option, as the Jumping Ability and Leap In let you easily get into position for a widespread Shockwave. Jumping Vigilance lets you easily get in position to heal or hand out Weakness tokens, then jump away to safety. You can trigger your Abilities in any order, so at the end of your turn, you can either use the Vigilance Ability before jumping away, or after jumping to an enemy.

styles.name: Rallying
abilities: At the start of each ally's turn, if they are within Range of you or your Copies, they may heal.
At the end of your turn, choose an ally you can see other than yourself. They heal and gain Shield 2.

actions.name: Group Up
actions.text:
Pull up to 3 to one ally you can see.
3+: Pull up to 3 to one ally you can see.
5+, Once per turn: Choose one to apply to each ally within range: Heal; -or- Gain 2 Power tokens; -or- Gain Shield 3.

styles.description: Rallying Style is healing focused, capable of picking your whole team back up off the ground. You are your own ally who is within your range, so the Rallying Abilities will heal you at the start and end of your own turn, and a 5+ Group Up will affect you as well as any allies pulled into range.
styles.recommended: Rallying Song and Rallying Vigilance are obvious, as the primary healing Forms. If you want an excellent support stance, look no further. Rallying Iron gives you Armor and access to Secure, which combos well with Group Up. The self-healing of the Rallying Ability also combines with Iron to create a powerful desperation stance, where you know you can get back up and you will likely stay up until your next turn. Rallying Shadow lets you get into position to heal your allies on their own turns, greatly improving the flexibility of the Rallying Ability. Being able to Stunt out of danger is also a good tool for a healer to have. Rallying Blaster and Rallying Control increase your Range, greatly improving the Rallying Ability's flexibility. Blaster's extra target can let Group Up pull an extra ally within range of your healing, while Control tokens allow you to actively protect your team with your massive Range.

styles.name: Unbreakable
abilities: Your allies within range may spend your tokens.
At the start and end of your turn, give 1 Iron token to each ally within range.

actions.name: Eyes Open
actions.text: You gain 4 Iron Tokens and may Move 1.

actions.name: Stay Out Of This
actions.text: Give 3 Weakness tokens and Push 3 to an enemy within range.

styles.description: Unbreakable Style lets you buff your team by proxy. Any token you hold becomes a token your friends hold. You are your own ally, so the Unbreakable Start Ability will always give you an Iron token, too.
styles.recommended: Unbreakable Control is the obvious choice, increasing your range to make sharing tokens easier. The Unbreakable Ability also lets your allies use your Control tokens, letting you use them as a range boost. Unbreakable Power and Unbreakable Iron let you build up a lot of Power or Iron tokens, to share with the Unbreakable Ability. Unbreakable Shadow keeps their Speed tokens outside of your turn, letting your allies borrow movement as they need it. There is no better Stance for protecting your team from a ring-out. Unbreakable Song gathers many basic tokens to share with your allies. It spreads the love even more than Song Form normally does.

supers.name: Call In The Cavalry
supers.effect: Deal 2 damage to all enemies, then deal 2 damage to all enemies.
supers.description: The Cavalry's Alpha Super hits ALL enemies, whether you can see them or not. Whether this cavalry is your clan backing you up, your biker gang driving through the arena, your pirate crew firing the cannons, your herd of sheep trampling everyone, your military buddies sniping from afar, or something else is up to you - they will still find an opening and beat down on all enemies, before running off stage.

supers.name: Inspire Perfection
supers.effect: Remove up to 4 Status tokens from yourself and each ally you can see. Heal, give 2 Power tokens, and give 2 Iron tokens to each ally you can see, including yourself.
supers.description: The Cavalry's Delta Super provides an incredible amount of support, making it a great panic button. It is especially effective against opponents relying on Burning and Weakness tokens, but also provides a nice boon against foes relying on Challenges or Fatigue. But even if there are few Common Tokens to remove, giving two Power and 2 Iron tokens to yourself and each ally is no small benefit.

name: Cyborg
description: Cyborgs build power over time. They adapt to the threat in front of them, growing stronger, tougher, or faster, as needed. If you let a Cyborg build up, they will destroy you. Cyborgs is a Growth Archetype, using their constant flow of basic tokens to trigger powerful Unique Actions. They are good at everything, and only weak to being struck down before they can properly prepare. Cyborgs need to pay close attention to their token management. Basic Tokens are their bread and butter, and everything they do relies on keeping a stock of the tokens they need when they need them. With a variety of powerful Token Actions and an Ability that gives you the tokens you need, the Cyborg sets itself up for success. As long as you stay focused, the Cyborg can handle anything in front of them.
focused: At the start of your turn, you gain 3 Basic Tokens of one type, 2 Basic tokens of a different type, and 1 Basic token of the final type.
fused: At the start of your turn, you gain 2 Basic Tokens of one type, and 1 Basic token of each other type.
frantic: At the start of this turn, you gain 3 Basic Tokens of one type, 2 Basic tokens of a different type, and 1 Basic token of the final type.

actions.name: XYZ-BURST
actions.text:
You may pay for XYZ-BURST using 2, 3, 4, or 5 Basic Tokens. You heal X, then teleport Y, then deal Z damage to an enemy within range.
X is equal to the number of Iron tokens spent to pay for this.
Y is equal to twice the number of Speed tokens spent.
Z is equal to the number of Power tokens spent.
Usable once per turn, only during your own turn.

notes: The Cyborg Abilities give you many Basic tokens of each type. The Basic tokens are Iron tokens, Power tokens, and Speed tokens. Each choice in the Cyborg Abilities is exclusive. If a Focused or Frantic Cyborg chooses to gain 3 Power tokens, they cannot pick Power Tokens for the next two options. They must pick Iron or Speed. And if they choose to gain 2 Iron tokens afterwards, then they are forced to gain 1 Speed token, as it is the only type of Basic token remaining. The XYZ-BURST Archetype Action is the only Action in the game to use multiple different X values. Y and Z function the same as X normally does in other X Actions, but each variable's value is set separately. While that sounds really complicated, XYZ-BURST's effect is actually very simple. The healing effect scales with Iron tokens spent, the teleport distance scales with Speed tokens spent, and the damage inflicted scales with Power tokens spent to pay for XYZ-BURST. Easy!

styles.name: Armored
abilities: After you spend Iron tokens or trigger your Armor, you heal 1. This can heal a maximum of 3 HP per turn.
If an enemy discards your Challenge token using an enemy Action or Ability, the enemy who held the token gains 2 Weakness tokens.

actions.name: Hard Body
actions.text:
You gain temporary Armor.
6+: You gain 4 Iron tokens.

actions.name: You, Stay
actions.text:
Challenge an enemy within range. Give that enemy 2 Fatigue tokens.
5 Iron: Instead give them 4 Fatigue tokens. You gain Shield 3.
Usable once per turn.

styles.description: Armored Style is tough as nails. With each Iron token you hold negating two damage instead of one, you are very difficult to take down. Spending Iron tokens to use You, Stay or XYZ-BURST will heal you with the Armored Ability. Temporary Armor is used after all other Armor and only triggers once. Once your temporary Armor has triggered, it is lost. Temporary Armor is a binary - you either have it or you do not. You cannot have multiple instances of temporary Armor.
styles.recommended: Armored Iron is the obvious pair, giving you Armor and the Iron tokens to spend on You, Stay. Iron also gets you extra healing from the Armored Ability, compared to any other Form. Armored Vigilance is a powerful recovery Stance. With the Vigilance Ability picking you up, the Cyborg Ability giving Iron tokens, and the Armored Ability making each Iron token count, this combination all but guarantees you'll survive to your next turn to try something else. Like all Cyborg Stances, Armored Song is a valid option entirely because Song Form can give you whatever Basic Token you need.

styles.name: Incinerator
abilities: After you use a Power token to Enhance a Hit, give 1 Burning token to the target of that hit.
After you take damage from Burning Tokens, gain 1 Power token.

actions.name: Overclock
actions.text:
Gain 2 Power tokens and 1 Burning token.
5+: Gain 2 more Power tokens and 1 more Burning token.
Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Flamethrower
actions.text:
Deal 1 damage and give 1 Burning token to an enemy within range.
4 Power: Instead, deal 2 damage and give 2 Burning tokens, and also, Flamethrower now applies to each target adjacent to the initial target(s).
Usable once per turn.

styles.description: Incinerator Style is extremely aggressive, getting enemies out of your face and setting them on fire. Incinerator's Ability only gives one Burning token to a Power-boosted hit, no matter how many Power tokens you spend.
styles.recommended: Incinerator Power is the obvious stance to take, as it gives you easy access to more Power tokens to spend on Flamethrower. Incinerator One-Two and Incinerator Blaster give you more hits with each Action, giving you more opportunities to hand out Burning tokens with Incinerator's Ability. Incinerator Control has a very large range of 1-6, letting you use Incinerator as more of a zoning stance. With sudden off-turn pushes with Flamethrower, you can keep your foes away from where they want to be. Like all Cyborg Stances, Incinerator Song is a valid option entirely because Song Form can give you whatever Basic Token you need.

styles.name: Machine
abilities: At the start of your turn, you gain 1 Iron token.
You may spend your Iron Tokens as if they were Power tokens or Speed tokens.

actions.name: High Efficiency
actions.text:
Choose two: You heal 1; -or- you gain 1 Iron token; -or- you gain 1 Power token; -or- you gain 1 Speed token; -or- you deal 1 damage to an enemy within range.
4+: Choose all five instead.
8+: Replace all 1's in High Efficiency with 2's.

styles.description: Machine Style is a well-rounded Style that pairs well with any Form. A 4+ High Efficiency performs all five choices, in the order listed. An 8+ High Efficiency also performs all five, but at twice the value: you heal 2, gain 2 of each Basic Token, and deal 2 damage to an enemy within range.
styles.recommended: Machine Iron can gain more Iron tokens, allowing you to use them with the Machine Ability. Being able to use Iron tokens as Speed tokens completely removes Iron's usual mobility downside. High Efficiency does a lot at low cost, so Machine Shadow, Machine One-Two, and Machine Wild make the best use of this with their many Action Dice. Wild's extra Action Dice are conditional, which makes it a little more unreliable as a preparation stance, but you can gain Iron tokens for the once you couldn't get, which are effectively every token type. Machine Vigilance can guarantee a 4+ and 1+ High Efficiency, making it an excellent preparation Stance that impacts the battlefield now. Like all Cyborg Stances, Machine Song is a valid option entirely because Song Form can give you whatever Basic Token you need. You have little reason to choose a song other than Iron, though.

styles.name: Rocket
abilities: After you Push, you may Teleport to an empty space adjacent to the target of that Push.
At the start of your turn, you may Push 3 to an obstacle, ally, or enemy within range.

actions.name: Nitro Boost
actions.text:
Teleport 2, then gain 2 Speed tokens.
6+: Teleport 2, then gain 3 Speed tokens.

actions.name: Rocket Tackle
actions.text:
Push 2 to someone within range.
5 Speed: If they are an ally, they Move up to 3. If they are an enemy, Push 2 and deal 2 damage to them.
Usable once per turn.

styles.description: Rocket Style carries your allies to where they should be, and pushes enemies away from where they want to be. The Rocket Triggered Ability teleports you AFTER the Push is finished, allowing you to stick right next to them.
styles.recommended: Rocket Dance is incredibly mobile, letting you Throw someone, teleport to them, and take home a bunch of Speed tokens for your trouble. The ability to use an off-turn Rocket Tackle, or to teleport after any of your Dance Unique Actions, is also particularly excellent. Rocket Shadow can keep hold of your Speed Tokens for impromptu Rocket Tackle interrupts, letting you rescue allies in danger or push enemies away. Like all Cyborg Stances, Rocket Song is a valid option entirely because Song Form can give you whatever Basic Token you need.

styles.name: Syphon
abilities: At the start and end of your turn, you may choose 1 token you hold. Either replace it with a Power token, or gain another copy of it.

actions.name: Power Converter
actions.text:
Target a single token held by you or someone within range. Choose one or both: You steal the targeted token(s) from them; and/or replace the targeted token(s) with Power tokens.
6+: Power Converter instead applies to every token they hold of the targeted token's type.

styles.description: Syphon Style filters out excess tokens into more Power, letting you turn weakness into strength. A 6+ Power Converter will steal and/or replace every token of a single type held by your target. So if an ally has 3 Weakness tokens, you may turn them into 3 Power tokens.
styles.recommended: Syphon Power and Syphon Wild can efficiently use all the Power Tokens you gain from Power Converter. Syphon Blaster lets you remove more tokens at once. An Amplified 6+ Power Converter can remove 5 types of tokens from anyone with range, giving all of them back to you as Power tokens. Extra targets don't give you more choices - you must make the same choice for every target. Syphon Reversal can potentially steal your opponent's tokens the moment they gain them, before they even get to use them. Syphon Thorns guarantees you get a 6+ Power Converter each turn. Like all Cyborg Stances, Syphon Song is a valid option entirely because Song Form can give you whatever Basic Token you need.

supers.name: Draining Knuckle
supers.effect: Deal 3 damage to an adjacent enemy, and they discard all Basic Tokens they hold. Then, you gain 2 Power tokens, 2 Iron tokens, and 3 Speed tokens.
supers.description: The Cyborg's Alpha Super syphons away all of your foes' power, stripping them of their speed, power, and durability. It also takes some of that power for yourself. A well rounded and always reliable move.

supers.name: Drive Install
supers.effect: You gain 6 Power tokens, 6 Iron tokens, and 6 Speed tokens. For the rest of this fight, you can spend 1 more Power token and 1 more Iron token per hit. For the rest of this fight, you only discard 1 Speed token at the end of each turn, instead of 3 of them.
supers.description: The Cyborg's Delta Super grants you incredible power for the rest of the fight. While many Super Moves have a bonus that lasts until the end of the Round, Drive Install lasts for the entire fight, giving you a small but permanent edge over everyone else.

name: Demon
description: Demons are big bullies. They get their strength from making others weak. They drain your strength, toss you aside, and just when you think you've got the upper hand, they sneak in a surprise attack. Demons are an aggressive Archetype, focusing on picking off their enemies one by one. They stay on their feet by keeping their enemies off balance, and limiting their ability to counterattack effectively. They are excellent at Rushdown and solid Harriers, with their ridiculous mobility. Demons need to be wary of their enemy's capabilities, because they are relatively fragile. They rely on their tricks, their Fog and Weakness tokens and teleports, to avoid being punished for their aggressive antics. But what really makes a Demon vicious is their Chaos Tokens, which they can spend to take Actions out of turn. They need to keep track of the best time to use those tokens, because a key interruption can mean the difference between defeat and domination.
focused: At the end of your turn, you gain 2 Chaos Tokens.
At the start of each enemy turn, you may Pull yourself up to X spaces towards the active character, where X is the number of Chaos Tokens you hold.
fused: At the end of your turn, you gain 1 Chaos Token.
At the start of each enemy turn, you may Pull yourself up to X spaces towards the active character, where X is the number of Chaos Tokens you hold.
frantic: At the end of this turn, you gain 2 Chaos Tokens.
Until your next turn, at the start of each enemy turn, you may Pull yourself up to X spaces towards the active character, where X is the number of Chaos Tokens you hold.

actions.name: Devil Dive
actions.text: Teleport 3, then deal 2 damage to an enemy within range. Chaos Token: This Unique Token is only used by the Demon.

notes: You may spend a Chaos Token to take a Reactive Action, as if you had spent a 4. Any Action that could be taken by spending a 4 is a valid option for a Chaos Token Action. Chaos Tokens are usable only once per turn.

styles.name: Dark
abilities: You can see and target enemies through Fog.
At the end of your turn, place a Fog obstacle into your space.

actions.name: Darkness Dawns
actions.text: Place one or two Fog obstacles into empty spaces within range. You may teleport to an empty space within those Fog obstacles.

actions.name: Twilight Sorrow
actions.text: Each enemy standing within Fog gains 1 Weakness token and 1 Fatigue token. Then, you gain 3 Speed tokens.

styles.description: Dark Style lets you set up a lot of Fog to hide in, and punish any enemies who try to use it by handing them Weakness tokens. For Twilight Sorrow, enemies standing adjacent to Fog still count as being in Fog. Twilight Sorrow gives you the same number of Speed tokens as the number of Weakness tokens it hands out. The Dark Ability replaces any obstacle in your space with Fog.
styles.recommended: Dark Shadow can use Stunt to create more Fog. The Shadow Ability lets you keep your Speed tokens when you use Twilight Sorrow out of turn with a Chaos Token. Dark Blaster lets you place more fog with Darkness Dawns, as well as taking advantage of its Ability to target through Fog for unavoidable, long-range Shockwaves or Amplified Damage Actions. Dark Control increases your Range, so Darkness Dawns can take you farther, and you can use your Control tokens through the Fog you spread. Your enemies cannot do the same to you. Dark Vigilance loves the high range of Dark Style for the Vigilance End Ability and to use Bow Down from afar, and having the option to Stand Strong from within the safety of Fog.

styles.name: Ogre's
abilities: Your Throws may target any number of enemies within range.
After you perform an Action that inflicted Forced Movement on any enemies, you deal 1 damage to each enemy moved by that Action.

actions.name: Gate Guardian
actions.text: Pull 2 to all enemies you can see, then deal 1 damage to each enemy within range.

actions.name: Watch Your Step
actions.text: Target an enemy you can see that moved during this turn. You Push 1 and deal 2 damage to them.

styles.description: Ogre's Style relies on Throws to trigger Watch Your Step, and its Ability makes those Throws better and easier to use.
styles.recommended: Ogre's Dance is a powerful ruinous stance, as your wide-reaching Pulls and Pushes will remove basic tokens from each enemy affected. Ogre's Blaster can Throw a bunch of enemies, then use an Amplified Watch Your Step to hit all of them at once. Ogre's Control has Range: 1-5, letting you use one Throw Action on as many enemies as possible. Gate Guardian is also especially good with Chaos Tokens, for keeping enemies within range of your Control Tokens.

styles.name: Slasher
abilities: After an effect Pushes you, you may Pull yourself up to 2 towards the source of that Push.
At the end of every turn, you may Move 1, then you deal 1 damage to an enemy within range.

actions.name: Suddenly...
actions.text: Teleport into an empty space adjacent to someone who is alone, then if they are an enemy, you deal 1 damage to them. Someone is alone if nobody is adjacent to them.

styles.description: Slasher Style wants to be in the thick of things. You slowly stalk your foes at the end of every turn, slicing into whatever enemy you can get close to. If they run too far away, you can use your Chaos tokens to Suddenly... be back in position. The Slasher Ability deals damage every turn, not just your turn.
styles.recommended: Slasher Reversal and Slasher Shadow can move out of turn, letting you stick close to enemies you want to focus on with the Slasher Ability. Reversal is especially nasty for this, because they can't do anything about your inevitable victory without giving you a free Reactive Action. Slasher Power and Slasher Song give you Power tokens, so you can deal more damage with the Slasher Ability. Slasher Iron and Slasher Thorns gives you the survivability you'll need to stand next to your enemies for several turns, and Contain can pull them close and place Traps for them to fall in while escaping from you.

styles.name: Vampire
abilities: After you deal damage with an Action or Ability, you heal 1. This Ability cannot heal you more than the Bleed Value in a single turn.
After you give Weakness tokens to an enemy, you gain 1 Power token, to a maximum of 4 Power tokens per turn.

actions.name: Life Steal
actions.text: Deal 2 damage and give 1 Weakness token to an enemy within range.

actions.name: Hypnotic Gaze
actions.text: Target an enemy you can see. Pull them up to 4, then if they are now within your range, give them 2 Weakness tokens.

styles.description: Vampire Style drains power with every blow, growing stronger as your enemies grow weaker. There is no better means of winning a game of Attrition than literally stealing HP and damage from your enemies.
styles.recommended: Vampire One-Two and Vampire Blaster have several multi-hit options, letting the Vampire Ability heal you more. Vampire Vigilance has many ways to give out Weakness tokens, which all turn into extra Power. Vampire Thorns deals 1 damage each time an enemy hits your Shield, which triggers the Vampire Ability's heal. If you put up your Shields while you are already damaged, enemies trying to break you will only help to heal you up again.

styles.name: Zombie
abilities: After an enemy destroys any of your Copies, you deal 1 damage to them.
At the start of your turn and when you Bleed, place a Copy into a space within range of you or your Copies.
At the end of your turn, you deal 1 damage to each enemy adjacent to any of your Copies.

actions.name: Hunger
actions.text: One target within range discards 3 tokens of their choice (or all of their tokens, if they have less). For each token they discarded, place a Copy into an empty space adjacent to them.

actions.name: Raise The Dead
actions.text: Give 2 Fatigue tokens to an enemy within range, then place 2 Copies in empty spaces adjacent to that enemy.

styles.description: Zombie Style is focused on aggressive defense, dealing damage with your throwaway cannon fodder as you throw more and more at them. You will drown the field in a sea of zombies Copies, and anyone trying to stem the flow will suffer harm for doing so.
styles.recommended: Zombie Shadow lets you place Copies with Stunt, as well as enabling out of turn movement, so you can more easily keep foes within range of the Zombie Ability. Zombie Vigilance is a durable stance that plays up the immortality of a zombie, reviving you at the start of your turn. Zombie Thorns puts your foes in a lose-lose position. They can go after your Copies and suffer harm for doing so, or go after you and take damage anyway!

supers.name: Unending Despair
supers.effect: Target an adjacent enemy. Give them 4 Burning tokens, 3 Fatigue tokens, and 2 Weakness tokens. You gain 2 Iron tokens, 2 Power tokens, 2 Speed tokens, and 2 Chaos tokens.
supers.description: The Demon's Alpha Super does not deal damage directly, but it instead heavily cripples a single foe and steals their power for yourself. A truly cruel despair, snatching away any hope the enemy has of winning.

supers.name: Dancing Mad
supers.effect: Teleport 3, then deal 2 damage to an adjacent enemy. You may repeat this as many times as you like. After you damage the same enemy twice, you deal 1 damage to all enemies within Range 1-3, then this Super Move ends.
supers.description: A dance of death. The Demon's Delta Super teleports madly around the map, damaging as many enemies as you can reach. Once you hit someone twice with this Super Move, you end with a dramatic flourish that deals 1 damage to everything near you. A flashy but difficult to execute Super Move.

name: Flametongue
description: Flametongues want to watch the world burn. They specialize in fire, explosions, and blasts of all sorts, destroying the terrain around them as they fight. They hand out a lot of Burning tokens, which deal more and more damage the more of them your enemies have. Flametongues are vulnerable to foes who can remove tokens easily. The Angel's Purify, the Cyborg's Power Converter, and the Trickster Ability can turn your blistering heat into their own strength. Also, Burning Tokens don't trigger until the end of their turn, and everyone can use Put It Out!, so don't rely solely on Burning Tokens to finish your foes off. The main way a Flametongue defeats their foes is by giving them more to deal with than they can reasonably handle. You give out so many Burning tokens, and lay out so many Traps, and punish them for hitting you, and just make fighting back the last thing they can afford to do.
focused: Three times per turn, after you deal damage to an enemy, give them 2 Burning tokens.
fused: Three times per turn, after you deal damage to an enemy, give them 1 Burning token.
frantic: Until your next turn, three times per turn, after you deal damage to an enemy, give them 2 Burning tokens.

actions.name: Incinerate
actions.text:
Deal 1 damage and give 1 Burning token to an enemy within range.
5+: Deal 2 damage and give 2 Burning tokens instead.
8+: Deal 3 damage and give 3 Burning tokens instead.

notes: The Flametongue Abilities not only give Burning tokens to your enemies, they also accelerate how rapidly they burn. Your enemies don't just take Burning damage on their own turn, they also take burning damage at the end of YOUR turn. Triggering Burning Tokens: During the End Phase, if the active character has any Burning tokens, they take damage equal to the number of Burning tokens they hold. Then, they discard half of their Burning tokens, rounded up.

styles.name: Blazing
abilities: At the start of each allied turn, give 1 Burning token to each enemy within range.

actions.name: Blazing Speed
actions.text:
Target an enemy you can see that has Burning Tokens. Pull yourself up to X spaces towards them, where X is the number of Burning Tokens they hold.
Usable once per enemy turn.

actions.name: Ignition
actions.text:
Deal X damage to an adjacent enemy. X = the number of Burning tokens they hold.
Usable once per turn.

styles.description: Blazing Style hands out Burning tokens to anyone who sticks too close to you. Even if they try to escape, Blazing Speed allows you to use your burnt enemies for mid-turn mobility, catching up to keep the Burning tokens building. Once enough Burning Tokens are in play, Ignition is a powerful finisher, burning down an enemy's HP all at once.

styles.name: Explosion
abilities: After you perform an Action that destroyed any obstacles, deal 1 damage to all enemies on or adjacent to any of those obstacles.

actions.name: Demolition
actions.text:
Choose one: Place a Pit into a space within range; -or- place 2 Traps into spaces within range; -or- destroy up to 3 obstacles within range.
5+: Choose two instead.
7+: Choose three instead.

actions.name: Ka-Boom!
actions.text:
Place Rubble into an adjacent space, then destroy it. Push yourself 2 spaces away from that Rubble.
4+: Place Rubble into an adjacent space, then destroy it. Push yourself 2 or 3 spaces away from that Rubble.
6+: Place Rubble into an adjacent space, then destroy it. Push yourself up to 3 spaces away from that Rubble.

styles.description: Explosion Style creates shrapnel. It tears the map apart, and shards of terrain will hurt any enemies standing too close to the chaos. When you place a Pit directly under an enemy, they immediately take 2 Fall damage unless they can Save Themselves. The Explosion Ability only triggers once per Action. If you destroy 3 obstacles adjacent to a single enemy, that enemy only takes 1 damage. Conversely, if you destroy 1 obstacle adjacent to three different enemies, all three of those enemies take 1 damage.

styles.name: Inferno
abilities: You have Armor against damage from Burning tokens.
After you Reduce a Hit, give 1 Burning token to your attacker.

actions.name: Flame Guard
actions.text:
You can only use Flame Guard while you hold no Iron tokens. You gain 2 Iron tokens.
Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Heat Beam
actions.text: Unblockable. Deal 3 damage to an enemy you can see that is holding at least 2 Burning tokens, then they discard 2 Burning tokens.

styles.description: Inferno Style involves setting yourself on fire to discourage enemies from attacking you. That's just smart. Like all Token Actions, Flame Guard can be used as a Reactive Action on anyone's turn. If you want to use Heat Sink early, you should start combat in Inferno, but don't take the first turn. Use Flame Guard during others' turns to build up Iron and Burning tokens, then get rid of those tokens for value with Heat Sink.

styles.name: Phoenix
abilities: At the start of your turn, you gain Shield 2, then if you are Bleeding, you heal.
When you Bleed, you heal and gain Shield 3.
You do not take damage from Burning Tokens.

actions.name: Cleansing Fire
actions.text:
Choose two: Give 2 Burning tokens to an enemy within range; -or- heal an ally within range; -or- discard up to 3 status tokens from an ally within range.
Usable once per turn.

actions.name: Firebird's Flight
actions.text: Teleport 3, then give 2 Burning tokens to all adjacent enemies.

styles.description: Phoenix Style rises from the ashes, returning you to life from the brink of defeat. Also, its immune to fire, which is a nice bonus. The Phoenix Ability heals you half as much damage as the Burning tokens would have dealt. So if you held 3 Burning tokens, you would heal 2 when they trigger. If you held 9 Burning tokens, you would heal 5.

styles.name: Volcanic
abilities: At the start and end of your turn, you may place a Trap into a space within range.
After an enemy within range takes damage from a Trap, give that enemy 1 Burning token.
You do not take damage from Traps.

actions.name: Lava Walk
actions.text:
Move 1, then place a Trap into the space you left.
Usable twice per turn.

actions.name: Pyroclasm
actions.text: Place 3 Traps into spaces within range.

styles.description: Volcanic Style covers the world around you with fire. Traps within your range are scarier than usual, giving Burning tokens to anyone they successfully deal damage.

supers.name: Erupting Burning Fist
supers.effect: Deal 4 damage and Push 4 to an adjacent enemy, then give them Burning Tokens until they hold 6.
supers.description: The Flametongue's Alpha Super deals incredible single target damage. Not up front, but the incredible burn left by your touch destroy them quickly.

supers.name: Watch The World Burn
supers.effect: Place a Trap under each enemy you can see, then give each of those enemies 2 Burning tokens and 3 Fatigue tokens. An unavoidable flame that burns everything.
supers.description: The Flametongue's Delta Super creates an eruption of flame underneath every enemy, trapping and burning them all equally. In fights against many foes, this is an absolutely devastating Super Move that forces your foes to make difficult choices on who gets to escape their fire traps first, and who is left to burn.

name: Gunkata
description: Gunkata is the ancient combat art of shooting people. Usually with guns. Ideally in the face. Probably a lot. Gunkata is a high-damage Archetype that hits its enemies over and over and over. They embody the idea of death by a thousand cuts, and they do it all from fairly far away, making them phenomenal Harriers. Big downside: your Styles have to deal with a minimum range. You need to be very wary of putting obstacles between you and your targets. Fog completely shuts you down and Walls make life difficult, but Rubble and Traps make it harder for your enemies to punish your ranged pokes. Gunkata has a weapon for every occassion. Play to your strengths and punish their weaknesses, and you'll find that victory is an easy target. Gunkata have 2 Archetype Actions: Grape Shot and Slug Shot.
focused: At the start and end of your turn, you perform one Gunslinger Action of your choice without paying its cost, from among those available to you in your current Stance.
fused: At the start -or- end of your turn, you perform one Gunslinger Action of your choice without paying its cost, from among those available to you in your current Stance.
frantic: At the start and end of this turn, you perform one Gunslinger Action of your choice without paying its cost, from among those available to you in your current Stance.

actions.name: Grape Shot
actions.text: This is a Gunslinger Action. Deal 1 damage to up to four enemies within range. Any target that takes 0 damage from Grape Shot is pushed 1 space.

actions.name: Slug Shot
actions.text: This is a Gunslinger Action. Push 4 and deal 2 damage to an enemy within range.

notes: "Gunslinger Actions" are labeled as such in their description. Each Gunkata Style has one Gunslinger Action unique to it. Your free Gunslinger Actions from the Gunkata Abilities do not count towards the once per turn Action limit of Reversal Form.

styles.name: Akimbo
abilities: At the start and end of your turn, Move 2.
After each Action you perform, Move 1.

actions.name: Firing Wild
actions.text:
Choose one: Deal 1 damage to each adjacent enemy; -or- deal 1 damage to up to 3 enemies within range; -or- deal 1 damage to up to 2 enemies you can see beyond your maximum range.
5+: Choose two instead.
8+: Deal 2 damage instead.

actions.name: Kneecapper
actions.text: This is a Gunslinger Action. Choose one or two enemies within range. Deal 1 damage and give 2 Fatigue tokens to each target.

styles.description: Akimbo Style hits the ground running, firing wildly at your foes then disengaging beyond their reach. The Akimbo Abilities are not optional. At the start of your turn, the end of your turn, and after each Action you perform, you must Move.

styles.name: Crosshair
abilities: Whenever you deal 3 or more damage to an enemy in a single hit, they gain 1 Weakness token and you gain 1 Power token.

actions.name: Take Aim
actions.text: This is a Gunslinger Action. Your next damage-dealing Action is Unblockable by Armor, Iron Tokens, and Shields.

actions.name: Headshot
actions.text:
Deal 5 damage to an enemy within range.
Usable once per Round.

styles.description: Crosshair Style keeps your enemies in your sights, ignoring their defenses and hitting them where it hurts, as long as you can keep them within your narrow range.

styles.name: Fullmetal
abilities: At the start of your turn, choose your Ammo: Incendiary, Toxin, or Tracer. You have the chosen Ammo effect until your next turn.
Incendiary: After each damage-dealing Action you perform, give each enemy dealt damage by that Action 1 Burning token.
Toxin: After each damage-dealing Action you perform, give each enemy dealt damage by that Action 1 Weakness token.
Tracer: You can see and target enemies through Fog and Walls. You have +2 maximum Range.

actions.name: Bombardment
actions.text: This is a Gunslinger Action. Place a Trap into any space within range. Then, deal 2 damage to each enemy adjacent to, or on, that Trap.

actions.name: Bazooka
actions.text: Deal 4 damage to an enemy within range, then deal 1 damage and give 2 Burning tokens to an enemy adjacent to you.

styles.description: Fullmetal Style has a toolbox of unique ammo types, granting you exactly the tool you need to handle your current enemies. Toxin ammo to weaken dangerous foes, Tracer ammo to pick out foes in hiding, and Incendiary ammo to pile the damage on when you don't need the other two types of ammunition.
styles.recommended: Fullmetal Control can either have a massive Range of 3-9, letting you hit just about anyone on the map, or close off your weakness to close range combat by making your Range 1-6. ~Coming Soon~

styles.name: Quickdraw
abilities: Add d6 to your Action Dice.
If an enemy discards your Challenge token using an enemy Action or Ability, the enemy who held the token gains 2 Fatigue tokens.

actions.name: Point Blank Shot
actions.text:
Push 1 and deal 1 damage to an adjacent enemy.
4+: Instead, Push 3 and deal 3 damage.

actions.name: Showdown
actions.text:
This is a Gunslinger Action. Challenge an enemy within range. If they take the next turn for their side, they cannot discard your Challenge before the end of that turn. If they do not, you deal 3 damage to them.
Usable once per turn. Unblockable by Shields.

styles.description: Quickdraw Style lets you do just a little bit more with any Form, making it a universally solid Style. Thanks to Point Blank Shot, you don't even need to worry about adjacent enemies escaping your range.

styles.name: Ricochet
abilities: After each Action you perform, you may choose one: deal 1 damage to one enemy within range that was not targeted by that Action; -or- replace one obstacle you can see with Rubble.

actions.name: Trick Shot
actions.text:
Choose one obstacle within range. Destroy it, then deal 2 damage to an enemy within Range 1-3 of that obstacle.
6+: Then, deal 2 damage to an enemy within Range 1-3 of that first enemy.
9+: Then, deal 3 damage to a third enemy within Range 1-3 of that second enemy.

actions.name: Scatter Shot
actions.text: This is a Gunslinger Action. Place Rubble into a space within range. Then, each enemy on or adjacent to that Rubble takes 1 damage and is pushed 3 spaces away from that Rubble.

styles.description: Ricochet Style spreads your damage around rapidly, letting you remove problematic obstacles and soften up many enemies at once. Trick Shot draws line of sight from the obstacle you chose with Trick Shot, instead of drawing from you. After each Gate, you draw line of sight from the enemy you hit with the previous part of Trick Shot, allowing you to shoot around corners. Trick Shot can shoot through Walls and Fog, by using the Wall or Fog in your way as your target. If you choose a Wall or Fog as the targeted obstacle, any enemy within 3 spaces of that Wall or Fog is a legal target, even if you couldn't hit them normally. If you place your Scatter Shot Rubble directly onto an enemy, the first space of their Push 3 can be in any direction. From there, the remaining two spaces must be away from the Rubble. This gives tons of flexibility on where you want to reposition an enemy.

supers.name: Sniping Point
supers.effect: Your maximum range is infinite, until the end of this Round. Then, deal 7 damage to an enemy within range.
supers.description: The Gunkata's Alpha Super sets you up in a high vantage point, from which you immediately fire a devastating critical shot. You get to keep the range increase for the rest of the round.

supers.name: Lead Rain
supers.effect: Choose an enemy within range. Deal 1 damage to that enemy and all adjacent enemies, then deal 1 damage to that enemy and all adjacent enemies, then deal 1 damage to that enemy and all adjacent enemies, then deal 1 damage to that enemy and all adjacent enemies, then deal 1 damage to that enemy and all adjacent enemies.
supers.description: The Gunkata's Delta Super is an unending barrage of gunfire. If nothing else works, try more gun.

name: Phantom
description: main gimmick is granted by their Poltergeist Tokens, which give them the Ability to modify their Actions as they perform them, changing and twisting them to accomplish what they could not before. Phantoms lack power. You need to rely on your team to actually defeat most foes, as the Phantom's Styles don't have any damage dealing Abilities or hard hitting Unique Actions. Phantoms have an answer to every problem, and can control the battlefield as you see fit. The outside of the ring is your friend, and tossing enemies out of bounds is child's play to a Phantom.
focused: At the start of your turn, you gain 4 Poltergeist Tokens.
fused: At the start of your turn, you gain 2 Poltergeist Tokens.
frantic: At the start of this turn, you gain 4 Poltergeist Tokens.

actions.name: Telekinesis
actions.text:
Choose one: Push 3 to an enemy or obstacle within range; -or- Pull 3 to an enemy or obstacle within range. If this movement ends with an enemy and an obstacle sharing a space, you deal 1 damage to that enemy.
Usable once per turn.

notes: Telekinesis is in the interesting position where you can spend 1 Poltergeist Token to pay for it, then 2 more to enhance it. Since you spent 3 Poltergeist Tokens on a single Action, you get to choose 3 Poltergeist Options that each have an X value of 3. In addition, you will always have spent 1 Poltergeist Token to use Telekinesis, so you will get to pick one Poltergeist Option with an X value of 1, even if you don't enhance Telekinesis at all. Poltergeist Token: This Unique Token is used by the Phantom. When you pay the cost of an Action, you may spend Poltergeist Tokens to modify that Action. You can spend up to 2 additional Poltergeist Tokens per Action. If you spend multiple Poltergeist Tokens on an Action, each choice must be different. All modifications made using Poltergeist Tokens are considered to be a part of the Action they modified, and will trigger Abilities as such. X is equal to the number of Poltergeist Tokens spent on this Action. Choose X: • Increase the value of up to X different numbers listed in this Action by 1. This option cannot increase Damage or Choices. ("Choose 2" cannot become "Choose 3", and "Deal 2 damage" cannot become "Deal 3 damage") • Increase this Action's maximum Range by +X. • Start of this Action: you teleport X. • Start of this Action: place Rubble into X spaces within range. • End of this Action: deal 1 damage to X enemies within range. • End of this Action: Push 1 or Pull 1 to X previous targets of this Action. If you spend 2 Poltergeist Tokens on an Action, not only is the Action improved with 2 choices, but X = 2 for each of those choices as well. Do you spend your tokens in bursts for maximum power output, or save some for Telekinesis to disrupt your foes' plans? Or do you do both, and fully enhance your Telekinesis for maximum Poltergeist power? Reminder: Placing Rubble into a space will remove all other obstacles that were in that space. The final Poltergeist option (Push/Pull 1) can be applied to any targets of the Action. This includes targets given by Poltergeist modifications, such as Rubble placed or enemies damaged.

styles.name: Aura
abilities: At the start of your turn, you gain Shield 3.
After an enemy within range damages or breaks an ally's Shield, or has their own Shield damaged or broken, you may Push 1 or Pull 1 to that enemy.
After a Shield within range breaks, you gain 1 Power token.

actions.name: Aura Surge
actions.text: Choose one: 1 ally within range gains Shield 3; -or- Remove up to 4 points of Shield from 1 enemy within range. If this breaks their Shield, deal 2 damage to them.

styles.description: You always count as an ally within range of your own Actions, so Aura Manipulation can give yourself a Shield. Aura Style is a shield-based support Style that punishes enemies who try to attack your team. You both crush enemy shields and bolster allied shields with supreme ease. If you pay for Aura Surge with 1 Poltergeist Token, you will get to pick one Poltergeist Option with an X value of 1.

styles.name: Crying
abilities: At the start of your turn, give 1 Weakness token to all enemies within range.
At the end of your turn, Challenge an enemy within range and give them 1 Weakness token.
If an enemy discards your Challenge token using an enemy Action or Ability, the enemy who held it gains 3 Burning tokens.

actions.name: Banshee's Wail
actions.text: All enemies within range gain 1 Weakness token and take 2 damage. All Traps, Pits, and Walls within range become Rubble.

styles.description: Crying Style weakens all of your enemies at once, while also calling out one specific enemy as the focus of your wailing rage.

styles.name: Puppet's
abilities: After each space you move using Free Movement, you may Move 1 to one ally or obstacle within range. Obstacles you move with this Ability become Rubble.
At the end of your turn, each enemy that moved this turn takes 1 damage, and each ally that moved this turn heals 2.

actions.name: Pull The Strings
actions.text:
Target an enemy or ally you can see. Pull them 3.
4+: Target an enemy or ally within range. Push them 3.
7+: Target an enemy or ally within range. Choose one: Push them up to 4; -or- Pull them up to 4.

styles.description: Puppet's Style can re-arrange the battlefield however you see fit. The second Puppet Ability will heal yourself, if you moved during your turn.

styles.name: Spirit
abilities: You and your Copies do not take damage from Pits or Traps.
You and your Copies treat Walls as if they were Rubble.
After each space of Free Movement you do, any number of your Copies may Move 1.

actions.name: Now You See Me...
actions.text:
Place a Copy into an empty space within range.
3+: Place a Copy into an empty space within range.
5+: Place a Copy into an empty space within range.
7+: Each of your Copies may Move up to 3.

actions.name: ...Now You Don't
actions.text:
Swap spaces with one of your Copies.
Usable once per turn.

styles.description: Spirit Style is a defensive style, letting your move freely while hiding yourself behind a wall of Copies. Your foes will never be able to tell which one is you, when you can swap spaces with a Copy in an instant.

styles.name: Vortex
abilities: You do not take damage from Pits.
When you are standing on a Pit, every other Pit counts as an adjacent space you can move to. Your range is still calculated only from the space you are currently standing in.

actions.name: Wormhole
actions.text:
Place a Pit into your own space.
4+: Place 1 Pit into an empty space you can see.

actions.name: Black Hole
actions.text: Target 1 empty space within range. Place a Pit into that space, then target someone within range and Pull them 2 towards the Pit.

styles.description: Vortex Style opens portals you can use to your advantage, both for mobility and as defense. Your movement defies all normal rules, and trying to catch you becomes a game of whack-a-mole. The Vortex Ability only counts for movement, not Range. You cannot stand on a Pit and attack any enemy within Range 1-2 of every other Pit. You must move through them first.

supers.name: Poltergeist Panic
supers.effect: You may move each Rubble or Trap you can see, up to three spaces each. Each must be moved into a different space - you cannot stack obstacles on top of each other. After you've finished moving obstacles, every enemy standing on an obstacle takes 3 damage, even if it wasn't an obstacle you moved onto them.
supers.description: The Phantom's Alpha Super is one of the strangest Alpha Super Moves, but is still much more straightforward than the Phantom Delta Super Move. Phantoms are just weird like that. This Super Move rearranges the battlefield entirely, and anyone you dropped an obstacle on top of takes 3 damage for their trouble.

supers.name: Arcana Install
supers.effect: You gain 6 Poltergeist Tokens. Until the end of this Round, you can spend up to 3 Poltergeist Tokens per Action, instead of only 2 per Action. Until the end of this combat, at the start of your turn, you gain 2 Poltergeist Tokens.
supers.description: The Phantom's Delta Super does not deal any direct damage. Instead, it amplifies your Phantom Ability, granting you much greater manipulation of your Actions. When you spend 3 Poltergeist Tokens on an Action, you get to pick 3 options from the list, and X = 3 for each of those options.

name: Punk
description: more you bleed, the stronger you hit back on the rebound. The Punk knows that if you outlast your enemy, you win. The Punk's greatest weakness is biting off more than they can chew. Their Styles and Abilities encourage going aggro, and punishing any enemies who take the bait. But if you aren't careful, you'll wind up hurt. Bait doesn't live a long life. If you can take the heat, though, nobody hits back like a Punk. Once they give you a reason, nothing will hold you back.
focused: At the start of your turn, add X to your Action Pool.
X is equal to the damage on your current health bar, to a maximum of 13. If your health bar is full, X = 3.
fused: At the start of your turn, add X to your Action Pool.
X is equal to half the damage on your current health bar, rounded up, to a maximum of 9. If your health bar is full, X = 2.
frantic: At the start of this turn, add X to your Action Pool.
X is equal to the damage on your current health bar, to a maximum of 13. If your health bar is full, X = 3.

actions.name: I'm Still Here
actions.text:
Push 4 and deal 4 damage to an enemy within range.
13+: Push 7 and deal 7 damage instead.

notes: For example, if your Health Bar has 12 HP when full, and you currently have 7 HP, then you have 5 damage on your current health bar. The Focused and Frantic Punks will add a 5 to their Action Pool, while the Fused Punk will add a 3.

styles.name: Brawling
abilities: At the end of each turn you took damage, you gain Shield 2.
After your Shield absorbs, you gain 1 Power token.

actions.name: Tough It Out
actions.text:
Pay 1 HP, then gain a 3 point Shield.
9+: You instead pay 2 HP and instead gain a 7-point Shield.

actions.name: Jab
actions.text:
You cannot use Jab unless you have a Shield with value 2+. Push 1 and deal 1 damage to an adjacent enemy.
Usable once per turn.

styles.description: Brawling Style can keep up with the most vicious of foes, staying in the fight with pure willpower. The harder they knock you down, the more damage and status you can ignore.

styles.name: Flashy
abilities: After you roll your Action Dice, you may combine two of your numbers into a single, larger number. Then, you may split one of your numbers in half (one rounded up, the other rounded down). You cannot split a 1 - the split number must be 2 or higher.

actions.name: Show Off
actions.text:
Choose X: Move 1; -or- Pull 1 to an enemy you can see; -or- deal 1 damage to an enemy within range; -or- give 1 Burning token to an enemy within range; -or- give 1 Weakness token to an enemy within range; -or- give 1 Fatigue token to an enemy within range; -or- Challenge an enemy within range; -or- push 1 to an enemy within range; -or- gain 1 Iron token; -or- gain 1 Power token; -or- gain 1 Speed token; -or- heal 1; -or- gain Shield 1.
Usable once per turn.

styles.description: Flashy Style is all about doing more with less. It favors Forms with many dice to add together with the Flashy Ability. So you don't need to count them: Show Off has 13 options. If you pay for it using a 13, you get to go down the entire list.

styles.name: Knockdown
abilities: After you take damage from an Action, you deal 1 damage to each enemy that dealt damage to you. If that enemy holds your Challenge, you deal 2 damage to them instead.

actions.name: Slugfest
actions.text:
Move 1, then Challenge an enemy within range, then they deal 1 damage to you.
Usable once per turn.

styles.description: Knockdown Style loves a good fight, and gives it out as good as it gets. Enemies who rely on hitting you multiple times will regret it. If you use Armor or Iron Tokens or Weakness tokens to reduce the damage you take to zero, the Knockdown Ability does not trigger. They need to deal damage to you for you to hit them back.

styles.name: Mad
abilities: At the start of your turn, choose a Weapon: Club, Knife, or Pistol. You have the chosen Weapon's effect until your next turn.
Club: After each damage-dealing Action you perform, give each enemy dealt damage by that Action one Fatigue token.
Knife: Your Actions and Abilities are Unblockable by Armor and Tokens.
Pistol: You have +3 maximum Range.

actions.name: Weapon Throw
actions.text: Deal 1 damage and give 1 Burning Token to an enemy you can see, then Disable your current Weapon until your next turn and choose a new one to take effect.

actions.name: Slice & Smash
actions.text:
Deal 1 damage to up to 2 enemies within range.
5+: Deal 2 damage and Push 1 instead.
8+: Deal 3 damage and Push 2 instead.
11+: Deal 4 damage and Push 3 instead.

styles.description: Mad Style pulls a weapon on 'em. You don't need to play fair, you need to win. They can die mad about it.

styles.name: Taunting
abilities: After you take damage, you gain 1 Iron token.
After you take damage from an enemy with your Challenge, you may Move 1.
If an enemy discards your Challenge token using an enemy Action or Ability, you gain 2 Iron tokens.

actions.name: Is That All You Got?
actions.text:
Challenge an enemy you can see. You gain 1 Iron token.
6+: Challenge another enemy you can see, then gain 2 Iron tokens and heal 2.
12+: Challenge a third enemy you can see, then give each of those enemies 3 Weakness tokens and Push 2.

actions.name: Not Good Enough
actions.text:
This Action costs your Challenge token held by an enemy within range. You must discard one such token to pay for Not Good Enough. Not Good Enough targets the enemy who held the Challenge Token you spent to pay for Not Good Enough. Give them 2 Weakness tokens.
Usable once per turn. Not Good Enough gives out two less Weakness tokens than the number you spent on it. For example, if you spend a 9 to use Not Good Enough, you give them seven Weakness tokens. Spending a 1 or a 2 will give them zero Weakness tokens.

styles.description: Taunting Style is a big distraction, letting you Challenge your enemies while keeping enough Iron tokens to survive anything.

supers.name: Knuckle Sandwich
supers.effect: Deal 5 damage to an adjacent enemy, then give them 4 Weakness tokens and your Challenge token. Then, Push them 3.
supers.description: Eat this! The Punk's Alpha Super knocks them into next week, disorienting them and making you the only thing they can see clearly.

supers.name: Everybody, Get 'Em!
supers.effect: Deal 3 damage to an adjacent enemy. Then, each of your allies in play (other than yourself) may each deal 3 damage to one enemy within their range.
supers.description: The Punk's Delta Super is a coordinated assault, where you and your allies beat the crap out of whoever they can reach. Especially effective while all of you surround the Boss, but can also be rendered very ineffective by poor spacing or half your team being dead.

name: Teacher
description: Your age only holds you back a little bit. You're strong, but not as strong as you used to be, and your lessons hit harder than your fist nowadays. But if they would listen to their Teacher, those reckless fools can do anything. The Teacher is a support based Archetype that donates Actions to the rest of their team. You don't have much power yourself, although Elder Style lets you draw on the strength you once had. Your real strength is in how much more you let your team accomplish. The Teacher is a force multiplier, improving the output of everyone around them. While force multipliers should be taken out immediately to weaken the team, going down is part of your lesson plan. Once the Teacher falls, their Heroic Spirit kicks in to overdrive. The Teacher is patient, observant, and steady. They know a wide variety of interesting techniques from all sorts of powerful combat styles, and will share those techniques with allies who can stand as their equal.
focused: At the start of your turn, you gain 2 Mentor Tokens.
fused: At the start of your turn, you gain 1 Mentor Token.
frantic: At the start of this turn, you gain 2 Mentor Tokens.

actions.name: Remember Your Training
actions.text:
The active character heals 1, then performs a Unique Action available to their current Stance, without paying its cost. For the purposes of Gates or the value of X, use a value of 4.
Usable once per turn, only during allies' turns.
Usable while you are Taken Out.

notes: The Teacher Abilities will still give you Mentor Tokens while you are Taken Out. A Teacher who has been struck down is more powerful than you can possible imagine. You can use Remember Your Training during your own turn, to perform one Unique Action you know for free. Remember Your Training doesn't allow the active character to bypass Action limitations. For example, Extreme Violence is only usable once per turn. If you use Remember Your Training on an ally who has already used Extreme Violence this turn, they cannot choose Extreme Violence as their free Action. Mentor Token: This Unique token is only used by the Teacher. Mentor Tokens have the passive effect to improve your Heroic Spirit, letting you mentor your allies and improve their skills. Mentor Tokens may also be used to pay for Remember Your Training. Mentor Token Effect: If you are holding any Mentor Tokens, then when you give your Heroic Spirit, increase one of those numbers by 2. Then, repeat this for each Mentor Token you hold.

styles.name: Decoy
abilities: At the start of each enemy turn, you may pay 1 HP to Challenge the active character.
After you Challenge an enemy, you deal 2 damage to them.
If an enemy discards your Challenge token using an enemy Action or Ability, heal your nearest ally to them, other than yourself.

actions.name: Leave My Student Alone
actions.text:
Pull 2 and Challenge an enemy you can see.
Usable once per turn.

styles.description: Decoy Style draws enemy attention away from your students, punishing anyone who ignores your Challenge.

styles.name: Elder
abilities: The cost of all Actions you perform are reduced by 1 (to a minimum of 1+ or 2 tokens/HP/Shield).
The damage values of all Actions you perform are reduced by 1 (to a minimum of zero).

actions.name: Show You How It's Done
actions.text: Target a Unique Dice Action available to someone's current Stance in this fight, other than Show You How It's Done or an Action you targeted earlier during this turn. Perform that Action. For the purposes of Gates or the value of X, use a value of 4.

styles.description: Elder Style is a strange beast. It pairs well with any Form, but it also pairs with every other Form and Style you have, due to its Ability. For the purposes of Remember Your Training, while you are in Elder Style you have access to the Unique Actions of all of your Stances. Elder Style likes Forms with good Unique Actions it can use for free. Some of the best are Blaster Form's Amplify, Iron Form's Protect, Power Form's Crush, and Song Form's Sing Along. You do not need to pair Elder Style with these Forms to use these Actions. You just need to have these Forms among your Stances.

styles.name: Mastermind
abilities: You cannot perform Actions. Instead, you pay their costs, but make your allies perform them for you.
Each Action you take uses an ally's current location, range, and Stance bonuses as if they'd taken that Action themselves. You can only give Actions to allies you can see.
After each Action an ally performs during your turn, you may Move 1.

actions.name: Diabolical Plan
actions.text:
You teleport 2 and gain 1 Chaos Token.
9+: You teleport 2 and gain 1 more Chaos Token.

styles.description: Mastermind Style directs your allies, deciding what they do for them. You can also time their actions more directly, whispering Diabolical Plans for exactly when they should strike. While Mastermind does have a Range, it does not use it for any Actions under normal conditions. You will only use this Range for passive Abilities, or if Mastermind Style has its Ability Disabled somehow. Diabolical Plan gives Chaos Tokens to your team, since they perform the Actions you pay for. Once you give them the token, they decide when and how they wish to use it. You laid out the plan, but they have to implement it. Chaos Token: This Unique Token is normally used by the Demon. You may spend a Chaos Token to take a Reactive Action, as if you had spent a 4. Any Action that could be taken by spending a 4 is a valid option for a Chaos Action. The Action granted by a Chaos Token does not count towards the once per turn Action limit of Reversal Form. Chaos Tokens are usable only once per turn.

styles.name: Patient
abilities: You have Armor.
At the end of each allied turn, you gain 1 Iron token.
After you use Armor or Iron tokens to reduce the damage you would take, one ally you can see other than yourself may heal 1.

actions.name: Take Your Time
actions.text: You gain 2 Iron tokens and 1 Mentor Token. Other Actions cannot be used to perform Take Your Time.

styles.description: Patient Style knows they are not the star. The stars are the heroes you have taught. Patient Style buys them time, supporting and protecting your pupils until they are ready to win this fight. "Other Actions cannot be used to perform Take Your Time" means that you cannot use Take Your Time through the effect of other Actions, such as Seize The Moment and Remember Your Training.

styles.name: Training
